messages:
maria_sales: FYI KiteLabs is ready to start a 2-week POC — they want to test our new gale-70b-quant variant for summarization + embeddings. can SEs confirm model availability and perf?

ajay_se: Thanks Maria. I ran a quick compatibility sweep: gale-70b-quant is in the catalog but only in our dedicated pool in us-west-2 right now.

ajay_se: Latency: ~120ms p50 for 512-token summaries on a 4k KV cache setup. Embedding path uses the 6k-batched encoder, should be fine.

maria_sales: Customer asked about private deployment (VPC) + KMS for keys — any blockers there?

taylor_infra: VPC/private is supported, but current gale-70b-quant image hasn't been validated for air-gapped onprem operators. For VPC we need to enable the quant runtime image and set up ECR access. Should be 2 business days ops work.

nina_security: On KMS: we support customer KMS via our envelope flow. But KiteLabs' security questionnaire specifically asks for HSM-level attestations and FIPS compliance. We don't ship HSM attestation docs by default. Need to know if this is a hard blocker.

maria_sales: They marked it as preferred but said they could accept keys in their cloud KMS if we provide SOC2/ISO docs.

ajay_se: For model behavior: the quant variant truncates some internal float ops — we should run a short eval on their prompt set to check for quality regressions vs full-precision gale-70b. Can we spin a test harness?

oliver_product: I can run a 200-sample regression test overnight if Ajay provides the prompt set and reference outputs. Also can surface token-cost delta and expected throughput.

customer_kitebot: @maria_sales thanks — we can hand off a 200-prompt eval tomorrow morning. two asks: 1) SLA for POC (99.5% during business hours)? 2) rough cost estimate for 2-week dedicated trial with ~100 reqs/s.

maria_sales: Noted. Ajay/Taylor — SLA + cost?

ajay_se: For a short trial we can offer a best-effort 99.5% uptime on a dedicated reserved pool. Real SLA language needs Legal but engineering can commit to monitoring and a rollback plan.

taylor_infra: Cost ballpark: for a 2-week reserved mini-pool sized for 100 rps (assuming average 256 tokens per request) — estimate ~$18k-$25k including burst capacity and kv-cache sizing. I'll produce a more granular calc.

nina_security: On the questionnaire: if they need HSM attestation we need to loop in GRC. That will add lead time — estimate 3-4 weeks for compliance artifacts. If they can accept KMS + SOC2/ISO docs, we can proceed now.

maria_sales: I'll push them to accept KMS + SOC2 for the POC. Meanwhile Ollie, can you include the quant quality caveat in the POC plan?

oliver_product: Yep. I'll add a short risk section: "gale-70b-quant may show small semantic drift on edge cases; run the provided eval and we will fallback to full-precision variant if regressions >2% on key metrics."

ajay_se: Also note: we need to configure prefix KV caching for their long-context summarization to hit the latency targets. That's an ops ticket (will open).

taylor_infra: I'll open infra ticket INF-4721: attach ECR permissions, pool sizing, autoscale policy for trial. ETA 2 days.

customer_kitebot: Great — timeline looks ok. please send POC runbook + invoice estimate and we'll confirm tomorrow.

maria_sales: Will do. action items: 1) Ajay: run the 200-sample eval and post results. 2) Taylor: infra ticket + cost breakdown. 3) Nina: confirm which compliance artifacts we can provide immediately. 4) Ollie: POC runbook + risk note. I'll bundle and send to KiteLabs by EOD. :rocket:

ajay_se: Starting eval now, will share artifacts in this thread.

taylor_infra: INF-4721 created, linked to this thread.

nina_security: I'll DM GRC and list available SOC2/ISO docs, will update here.

maria_sales: Thanks all — keeping this thread as the single source for handoff.

(automated) deploy-bot: ticket INF-4721 assigned to taylor_infra
